texts.text: Weather Report

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Rain this week brought variable precipitation accumulations across Manitoba. Most regions received more than 8 mm of rain. Parts of the Southwest, Northwest, and areas around the southern edge of Lake Winnipeg received more than 30 mm. The highest accumulation of precipitation in the past seven days was at Miniota with 77.8 mm.
texts.text: Rain this week brought variable precipitation accumulations across Manitoba. Most regions received more than 8 mm of rain. Parts of the Southwest, Northwest, and areas around the southern edge of Lake Winnipeg received more than 30 mm. The highest accumulation of precipitation in the past seven days was at Miniota with 77.8 mm.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: · Climate normals for total accumulated precipitation from May 1 to September 20 range from 245 mm to 380 mm and are based on 30-year historical data. Since May 1, large areas of the Northwest and Southwest regions have accumulated more than 380 mm of precipitation. Seasonal accumulations are above normal for the majority of the Northwest and Southwest regions. Large areas of the Northwest, Southwest, and Interlake regions have seen accumulations over 130% of normal. A few localized areas of the Interlake, Central and Eastern regions have seen accumulations below 90% of the 30-year average.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Southwest
texts.text: Southwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Little to no harvest progress this past week due to rain and spotty showers. Water laying in fields makes travel difficult. Cool evenings and foggy mornings have resulted in dewy morning conditions. Producers with access to driers spent much of last week drying grain and trying to create room for wet grain, so that when they can get back in the field, they have places to store it. Some producers tested fields over the weekend, but fields and grain samples were very wet. In many areas standing and swathed crops are sprouting. Most areas are reporting severe lodging in all crops still to be harvested.

Some producers tested fields over the weekend, but fields and grain samples were very wet. In many areas standing and swathed crops are sprouting. Most areas are reporting severe lodging in all crops still to be harvested.

texts.label: text

texts.text: Winter cereal and field pea harvest is complete, with reports of average yields and good quality.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Spring wheat harvest is 40 to 45% complete, with average to above-average yields. Quality has been good in earlier-harvested crops, but downgrading is occurring in more recently harvested fields.
texts.text: Spring wheat harvest is 40 to 45% complete, with average to above-average yields. Quality has been good in earlier-harvested crops, but downgrading is occurring in more recently harvested fields.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Barley harvest is approximately 70% complete, with average to above-average yields. Quality has started to decrease due to recent rains, and producers are reporting concerns about sprouting. Recently, harvested crops were being downgraded due to sprouting, colour, and low test weight, with much of the crop being graded as feed.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Oat harvest is approximately 50% complete. Oat harvest is limited as many fields are still green, and wet conditions are making producers reluctant to swath.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola harvest remains limited, at less than 25% complete. Reports indicate average yields and good quality. Several fields are being swathed, mostly due to severe lodging caused by disease. Several fields are also being sprayed. Harvest conditions are difficult due to lodging and wet fields.

texts.orig: Northwest
texts.text: Northwest

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Precipitation at the beginning of the week held up harvest progress for most of the region. Low areas continue to hold water, creating challenging harvest conditions. Harvest was able to resume toward the end of the week and over the weekend. Heavy dews continue to narrow the harvest window. Sprouting is occurring in standing and swathed crops. While some post harvest operations are occurring as crops are harvested, some are waiting for drier conditions.

texts.label: text

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola fields continue to range in stages, with the majority of the crop nearing maturity. Desiccation and swathing is underway in fields that have reached the appropriate stage. Fields that experienced excess moisture have patches of delayed growth that are behind. Canola harvest is approximately 10% complete, with below average to average yields being reported.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Majority of soybeans are in the late R6 to R7 stage and are looking good where excess moisture didn't delay growth this spring. Stagey conditions are evident in some areas that experienced excess moisture through the season.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Central
texts.text: Central

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Harvest progression varies considerably across the region. The area surrounding Portage la Prairie has been impacted by excess rainfall in September and much of the spring cereal and canola crop remains in the field. Delays in harvest has led to several issues.
texts.text: Harvest progression varies considerably across the region. The area surrounding Portage la Prairie has been impacted by excess rainfall in September and much of the spring cereal and canola crop remains in the field. Delays in harvest has led to several issues.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: In most of the region, spring cereal harvest is almost at completion. Much of the harvested grain requires additional drying. Many of the later harvested cereal crops have lodging issues, and quality declines, including pre harvest sprouting issues. Across the entire region, spring wheat yields and protein percentages range from average to good. Barley yields are slightly above average. Oat test weights, however, are lower than typical, likely due to lower soil moisture during critical development stages.

Oat test weights, however, are lower than typical, likely due to lower soil moisture during critical development stages.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A small number of producers began soybean harvest early last week. Fields are at R7 (beginning maturity) through to R8. Due to dry and warm conditions earlier in the season, many plants have predominantly two-seeded pods, with very few four-seeded pods. Pod abortion has also occurred in the upper canopy in many fields. Many fields have areas of soybeans maturing at different rates, and this has made decisions regarding harvest timing difficult.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Pea harvest is complete. Quality has been good, while yields have been average, with a few fields that experienced more optimized soil moisture conditions showing above-average yields.
texts.text: Pea harvest is complete. Quality has been good, while yields have been average, with a few fields that experienced more optimized soil moisture conditions showing above-average yields.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Edible beans are being cut and pre-harvest herbicide applications are being applied. The earliest fields have been harvested.
texts.text: Edible beans are being cut and pre-harvest herbicide applications are being applied. The earliest fields have been harvested.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola harvest and swathing continue, with approximately 65% of the crop now harvested. Pre-harvest sprouting has been an issue in some fields. In general, yields have been lower than in recent years, likely a combination of early-season excess moisture and mid to later season dryness, hot and dry conditions at flowering, cabbage seed pod weevil, and verticillium stripe. Pod shattering and drop has been a common issue. Many fields have a strong carpet of volunteer canola.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Flax is at stage 12 (seed ripe), with stem colour changing and leaves dropping. Pre-harvest herbicides have been applied, and the earliest fields may begin to be harvested in the coming week if conditions allow. Overall, flax crops are good, aside from areas that had waterlogging early in the season, and there are a few patches within fields which will likely yield poorly.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Manitoba Sunflowers are late R8 (back of the head fully yellow, bracts remaining green), with the crop likely to approach physical maturity in the next week (R9, bracts becoming yellow and brown).

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Corn is at R5 (dent), with milk lines progressing 75% down the kernels. Corn silage harvest has begun, although high plant moisture and kernel integrity are concerns for this year's crop. The corn crop appears to have fared relatively well despite the dry conditions experienced earlier in the season. Blackbirds are feeding on cobs.

texts.text: Eastern

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Rainfall across the region over the past week continued to delay harvest. Very little harvesting happened over the last week as field conditions remained wet with few good drying days.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Wheat harvest is estimated at 95% complete. Oat harvest is estimated at 95% complete while barley is at 90% complete. All spring cereal yields have been reported as average at best. Damage from drowned out areas of fields earlier this spring have brought yields down.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The majority of corn is in the dent stage of kernel development; on average the milk line is at the 75% mark. The crop is continuing to grow well as starch accumulates in the kernel. Growers agree that enough moisture has fallen to finish up the crop. Producers are hopeful the frost stays away as the corn continues to accumulate starch and mature.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola harvest is where the most progress was made across the region this past week. Harvest is estimated at 75% complete, with some farms finished. Yields are below average to average. Hot and dry weather during the flowering period is being blamed for the average to below average yields along with the water damaged areas from earlier in spring.

texts.text: Interlake

texts.label: text

Excess moisture and heavy wind have caused lodging and concerns about grain quality. Yields and quality vary across the region due to differences in rainfall throughout the season. Frost in some areas has helped mature crops dry down.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Manitoba Corn silage chopping continues. Yields vary with seasonal rainfall, while early reports range from average to slightly above average. Grain corn is at R5, with frost related leaf browning evident in some fields.
texts.text: Manitoba Corn silage chopping continues. Yields vary with seasonal rainfall, while early reports range from average to slightly above average. Grain corn is at R5, with frost related leaf browning evident in some fields.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The majority of soybeans are at R7 to R8 and are dropping leaves. If weather permits, harvest will begin later this week. Pea harvest is nearly complete in most areas, with slightly above average yields.
texts.text: The majority of soybeans are at R7 to R8 and are dropping leaves. If weather permits, harvest will begin later this week. Pea harvest is nearly complete in most areas, with slightly above average yields.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Canola harvest is about 45% complete, with early yields ranging from below average to above average. Strong winds and rain reduced yields in some standing and swathed fields. Reseeded canola is performing better in areas that received timely early season rain.
